summary:
I inspected ~23 real sites across the three categories, reading raw page text and DOM where possible rather than relying on summaries. The headline finding is that Wiseman's problem is not the RentCafe platform — it is the information architecture sitting on top of it. Wiseman's entire top-level nav is "Home | Contact Us" plus utility links to Residents/Applicants; there is no About, no History, no Neighborhoods, no Careers, no Development/Owner section, and the Contact page is a bare five-field form with no address, hours, or department routing. Meanwhile Presidio Residences (presidio-residences.com), an award-winning site running on the exact same RentCafe/Yardi stack, has renamed /searchlisting to "Our Neighborhoods," added About Us and History pages, put a numbered interactive map of 25 named neighborhoods on the homepage with a Historic/Non-Historic toggle, uses the stock RentCafe property-type taxonomy to carry era tags ("APARTMENT, POST WWII", "DUPLEX/TRIPLEX, HOME, HISTORIC"), and runs a hero video of someone walking a dog down a tree-lined street instead of an amenity carousel. Essex Property Trust — a $15B+ REIT — also runs its resident portal on RentCafe (essexrentcafe.securecafenet.com) behind a fully custom front end. So "we're on Yardi" is not the constraint.

The second finding is that the standard IA for a portfolio operator of this size has converged on a stable five-block structure: (1) a single search/finder entry point, (2) a market → neighborhood → property hierarchy with real neighborhood pages, (3) a resident-services page distinct from the login link, (4) a company/legacy block, (5) a careers block, with owner/investor as an optional sixth. Every credible peer has at least four of the five; Wiseman has zero. The third finding is that for a company whose differentiator is longevity and local roots rather than scale or luxury, the winning pattern is already proven in LA by Decron (founder Jack Nagel, immigrant and Holocaust survivor, 1950s first development, stats bar of 60+ years / 300+ employees / 10,000+ units) and Goldrich Kest ("Welcoming You Since 1957," "A Legacy of Connection," 65+ years / 200+ properties / 500+ team members) — a named human origin story plus a hard-numbers proof bar plus explicit neighborhood naming. Irvine Company does the same at scale with a homepage block literally titled "forever ownership" citing 150 years. Notably, the biggest direct competitor by footprint, Douglas Emmett, does this badly: its apartments site's Locations page is a wall of SEO prose with the actual property list buried in the footer.
recommendations: Build a real top-level nav. The minimum credible set, based on what every peer at this size has: Find a Home (or Our Neighborhoods) | Neighborhoods | Residents | About (Our Story, History, Leadership, News) | Development | Careers | Contact — plus a utility bar with a single leasing phone number, Resident Login and Applicant Login. Moss & Company proves this is achievable inside the same RentCafe template Wiseman already pays for.

Relabel /searchlisting to 'Our Neighborhoods' or 'Find a Home', exactly as Presidio Residences and Moss & Company have done, and make it the primary header CTA on every page instead of the current 'CONTACT US' hero button.

Make neighborhood the first-class organising principle. Build seven neighborhood landing pages — West LA, Brentwood, Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City, Hollywood/Beverly Grove, Glendale — each with real place writing, a map, the Wiseman buildings in that area, and a link into the filtered finder. Copy Equity Residential's pattern of tagging every listing card with its neighborhood as the primary subtitle, above the street address.

Fix the finder before anything else. Synced numbered map + list (Equity), a neighborhood facet as the first filter, beds/baths/price/move-in/pets/parking/laundry filters, a 'Coming Soon' state, and either infinite scroll or a much larger page size — 25-of-72 pagination is the worst possible default for a portfolio this size.

Use RentCafe's property-type taxonomy to carry era and building-type tags the way Presidio Residences does ('POST WWII', 'HISTORIC', 'DUPLEX/TRIPLEX'). For a 45-year LA portfolio this turns a liability (mixed vintage) into the differentiator: a 1970s West LA courtyard building and the 2026 Motor Tides new-build are different products and should be filterable as such.

Collapse the three-tier property experience. Today a renter goes wisemanresidential.com → a RentCafe /apartments/... detail page (new tab) → a brocktonmanor.wisemanresidential.com subdomain. Pick one destination per property and keep the Wiseman header, colours and phone number on it. G.H. Palmer shows where the link-out-to-microsites road ends.

Consolidate to one central leasing number with intelligent routing, as Irvine (866.371.1063) and Presidio (844-808-6177) do. Six different numbers on one results page — including a 984 North Carolina area code — actively undermines the 'local operator' claim.

Build a Residents page, not just a login link. Model it on Essex's /current-resident: Pay Rent, Submit a Maintenance Request, Resident FAQs, Renters Insurance, Move-in/Move-out, and a resident contact form — with the portal login as one card among several rather than the only door.

Add an 'Our Story' plus 'History' pair. Name the founder and the year. Follow Decron's structure: a human origin story, then a hard stats bar. Wiseman's should read something like 45 years / 72 communities / N units / 7 neighborhoods / $X reinvested in capital improvements — that last number is what separates an owner-operator from an acquirer and no REIT can match it on a per-building basis.

Turn the service claim into checkable promises. Replace 'professional, communicative, and proactive' with three or four specific, ownable commitments in the mould of Bozzuto's '70-item checklist and a 30-day guarantee' or ila's named perks — e.g. a stated maintenance response window, a named property manager per building, a move-in standard.

Give the development/owner-operator side its own home. Add a 'Development' or 'Build With Us' section on the model of Sentral's 'FOR OWNERS & DEVELOPERS' block and Moss's 'Management Services / Due Diligence / Proposals' — a completed-projects list, the Motor Tides case study, and an inquiry form — so the developer identity is visible without intruding on the renter path.

Name and productise touring. Irvine's 'SELF-GUIDED TOURING' is a top-level nav item with a branded app; Wiseman currently mentions tours only in prose on the Motor Tides block. Add 'Schedule a Tour' as a persistent CTA alongside 'Apply' on every property card and detail page.

Add an interest-list capture for the 72-property reality: when a renter's filters return nothing, capture neighborhood, bedrooms, budget and move-in date (Irvine's form fields) rather than dead-ending. Presidio calls theirs a 'Housing Interest Form'.

Rebuild the footer as a full site map with the entire portfolio enumerated by neighborhood, the way Douglas Emmett, Bozzuto (22-state directory) and Irvine do. It is the cheapest SEO asset available and Wiseman currently has none.

Adopt transparent all-in pricing with a disclosure line, following Greystar's 'Total Monthly Leasing Prices, which include base rent and mandatory monthly costs.' This is becoming table stakes and is an easy trust win for a long-tenured local operator.

Replace the stock 15-slide carousel with place-led imagery of the actual streets and buildings. Presidio's hero is a video of someone walking a dog down a residential street; Moss's is the LA skyline at dusk captioned 'IT'S PERSONAL'. Wiseman's current alt text ('A modern living room with a fireplace and a large window') describes stock-feeling interiors that could belong to any operator anywhere.

Fix the count inconsistency before launch: the homepage claims 'over 100+ apartment communities' while the finder says 72. Pick the defensible number and use it everywhere, including in the stats bar.
donots: Do not claim the RentCafe/Yardi platform is the reason the site is generic. Essex Property Trust runs its resident portal on RentCafe SecureCafe behind a fully custom front end, and Presidio Residences — an award-winning site — is a RentCafe template with better IA. The constraint is the information architecture and content, not the vendor.

Do not copy the luxury-amenity voice of Irvine Company, Related Rentals or Sentral. Wiseman's differentiator is 45 years and local roots, not resort pools, concierge or member clubs; borrowing that vocabulary puts Wiseman in a comparison it cannot win.

Do not build an investor-first site. Cityview and CGI+ are investment managers whose sites speak only to LPs and give renters no path to a lease; Wiseman is owner + developer + manager and must serve renters first.

Do not proliferate per-property microsites. G.H. Palmer and (to a lesser degree) Goldrich Kest link out to standalone property sites, which means no brand or SEO equity accrues at the parent level. Wiseman already has three tiers; do not add a fourth.

Do not state unit counts, employee counts, dollars reinvested, or founding details I have not verified. I confirmed 72 properties on the live finder and the '100+ communities' claim on the homepage, and nothing else about Wiseman's portfolio; all legacy stats must come from the client.

Do not assert that Equity Residential and AvalonBay have merged or rebranded. I observed 'Vivmark Residential' in the equityapartments.com footer and Avalon/AVA/eaves properties on its Los Angeles page, but I did not verify any corporate transaction — the IA lessons stand independent of that.

Do not describe Presidio Residences, Moss & Company, Decron or Goldrich Kest as direct competitors in client-facing material. Presidio is a National Park Service trust in San Francisco; Moss is primarily a third-party manager; Decron and Goldrich Kest are larger and more diversified. They are peers and models, not rivals.

Do not treat Douglas Emmett's site as the bar to clear. It is the closest competitor by footprint but its apartments Locations page has no property list, no map and no filters — the actual portfolio only appears in the footer. Wiseman should be benchmarking against Equity's LA page and Presidio, not against DE.

Do not build a photo slider or a testimonial carousel as a substitute for content. Those are exactly the stock-template moves the current site already makes; the peers that read as credible replaced them with neighborhood pages, history pages and editorial guides.

Do not ship a Careers or Development page without real content behind it. Every peer at this size has one, but Sares Regis's homepage still carrying a COVID-19 Updates block shows that a stale section is worse than no section.

findings.title: Wiseman baseline: a two-item nav, a three-tier fragmented property experience, and eight different phone numbers
findings.detail: Read directly from the live DOM. The entire primary nav is: Home, Contact Us — plus a utility row of a phone link (+1 310-473-3000), "Residents" (→ wisemanresidential.securecafe.com/residentservices) and "Applicants" (→ .../onlineleasing). There is no About, History, Neighborhoods, Careers, Development, Owner Services, Blog, or Resident Services page. The homepage is: hero carousel (15 gallery slides, generic alt text like "A modern living room with a fireplace"), "Welcome to Wiseman Residential" prose block, a Motor Tides feature block, a four-card Featured Properties carousel, and a closing line. /contactus is a bare form (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Message, 512-char limit) with no office address, no leasing hours, and no routing between leasing / maintenance / owner / press inquiries. /searchlisting shows "72 PROPERTIES", "Showing 25 out of 72", tabs PROPERTIES / NEIGHBORHOOD, views List / Favorites / Demographics, and an unstyled RentCafe map of unlabeled pins. Every property card opens in a NEW TAB to a RentCafe detail page (/apartments/ca/los-angeles/<slug>/default.aspx), which in turn links out to a THIRD site — a per-property subdomain (brocktonmanor.wisemanresidential.com). Three brand tiers, two context switches, before a renter sees a floor plan. Cards carry per-property phone numbers: 310-867-1343, 310-473-3000, 310-699-7027, 323-570-4466, 310-279-6475, and 984-349-0025 — 984 is a North Carolina area code, which reads badly for a 45-year LA operator. Finally, the homepage claims "over 100+ apartment communities" while the finder says 72.

findings.title: Presidio Residences is the single most actionable model — same RentCafe stack, transformed into a heritage neighborhood brand
findings.detail: This is the closest thing to a proof-of-concept for what Wiseman should build, and it runs on the identical platform (page title literally ends "| RentCafe"). Nav: Home | Our Neighborhoods | About Us | History | Contact Us | Main corporate site — note that "Our Neighborhoods" points at /searchlisting, i.e. they relabeled the stock RentCafe search page. Hero is a VIDEO of a woman walking a dog down a tree-lined residential street, with three CTAs: "View Our Availability", "Housing Interest Form", "Learn About the Presidio". Homepage then has "Our Neighborhood" — a numbered interactive map listing 25 named neighborhoods (Pilots Row, North Fort Scott, Storey, Ruckman, Kobbe, Baker Beach, West Washington, Wyman, Infantry Terrace, Riley, Funston, Presidio Blvd, Simonds Loop, Quarry, MacArthur, Portola, Sanches, Liggett, Belles, Landmark…) with a Historic / Non-Historic toggle; then a "Presidio Living" place layer (Recreational Fun, Eat, Volunteer, Presidio Go Shuttle); then "Available & Coming Soon" with specific unit callouts ("Coming Soon! 746-A Three-Bedroom historic duplex home!"). Crucially, they hijacked RentCafe's property-type taxonomy to carry era/typology tags on the listing cards: "APARTMENT, TOWNHOUSE, POST WWII", "DUPLEX/TRIPLEX, HOME, HISTORIC", "TOWNHOUSE, POST WWII". The /history page is organised Pre-World War II / Post-World War II by architectural era (Victorian, Georgian, Mediterranean; "a Victorian built in 1889 that once served as officers' quarters") with a "View Neighborhoods" CTA back into the finder. They also added a per-property "Bird's Eye View" modal alongside the stock "Neighborhood" WalkScore modal.

findings.title: Moss & Company: the closest same-platform LA peer, one full tier above Wiseman with the same tooling
findings.detail: Southern California property manager, "PROFESSIONALLY MANAGED REAL ESTATE SINCE 1960!", 14,000+ residential units. Same RentCafe template family as Wiseman (same /index, /searchlisting, /contactus URL scheme, same accessiBe widget, same 'opens in a new tab' property cards). But the nav is a real IA: Home | Find Your Apartment | Commercial | Management Services (submenu: Management Services, Due Diligence / Proposals, Our Services, Our Experience) | Careers | About Us (submenu: About Us, Our Purpose, Leadership) | Contact | News. Hero is a dusk LA skyline with the logo and the tagline "IT'S PERSONAL" — a local-operator positioning, not an amenity shot. Homepage adds a NEIGHBORHOODS row above Featured Properties with six clickable areas: WESTSIDE / BEACH CITIES, SAN FERNANDO VALLEY, DOWNTOWN LA, ORANGE COUNTY, LOS ANGELES COUNTY, LONG BEACH — exactly the layer Wiseman is missing — plus a stats block (14,000+ residential units, 2M sq ft retail and office) and segment cards for Furnished and Student Housing. Note they renamed the search page "Find Your Apartment", again showing the RentCafe label is editable.

findings.title: Douglas Emmett — the closest competitor by footprint — splits corporate from apartments and does its Locations page badly
findings.detail: Douglas Emmett is the direct West-LA/Brentwood/Santa Monica/Westwood competitor (5,000+ apartment units, ~18M sq ft office). Corporate site nav: HOME | OFFICE PROPERTIES | APARTMENT COMMUNITIES | INVESTORS | OUR COMPANY, with footer groups covering Investors, Our Story, Our Team, DE Builders, Development, Careers, Blog. The renter-facing site is a separate domain, douglasemmettapartments.com, whose nav is HOME | LOCATIONS | ABOUT | CONTACT US | RESIDENTS (→ der.mriresidentconnect.com — MRI, not Yardi). NOTABLY BAD: the /locations/ page contains no property cards, no map, and no filters — just three paragraphs of keyword-stuffed SEO prose ("Looking for an apartment for rent in Santa Monica or a stylish apartment in Honolulu?"). The actual portfolio only appears in the FOOTER, grouped LOS ANGELES → SANTA MONICA (Pacific Plaza, The Shores, 1221 Ocean Avenue) / WESTWOOD (The Glendon) / BRENTWOOD (The Landmark Los Angeles, 555 Barrington, Barry Apartments, Kiowa Apartments, Barrington Kiowa Apartments), HAWAII → HONOLULU. Their corporate "Our Story"/"Our History" is pure text narrative, no timeline graphic, no photographs — 1971 founding, 2006 IPO, ~40% of Class A office in target LA submarkets. This is a large, real gap Wiseman can beat with very little effort.

findings.title: Essex Property Trust runs its resident portal on RentCafe behind a fully custom front end — the platform is not the constraint
findings.detail: Essex nav, read from the DOM: Home | Apartments | Retail | Careers | Investors (opens new window → investors.essexapartmenthomes.com) | Current Resident | Resident Sign In | Contact. The Resident Sign In link goes to essexrentcafe.securecafenet.com/residentservices/apartmentsforrent/userlogin — the same Yardi/RentCafe SecureCafe product Wiseman uses. Hero: "Always Right at Home" over a lifestyle photo with a single typeahead ("Search by community, city, state or zip") and three region chips: Northern California / Southern California / Seattle Metro. The /apartments finder offers nine metro chips (Los Angeles Area, Orange County Area, San Diego Area, Santa Barbara Area, Ventura County, East Bay Area, San Francisco Bay Area, South Bay Area, Seattle Metro) plus a genuine "Map only / List only" toggle over an embedded map. The /current-resident page is a clean template for what a resident hub should contain: Resident Portal, Resident Perks, High Speed Internet, Easy Online Payments (24/7 self-service, auto-pay), Maintenance Requests (portal or Resident App), Resident FAQs, Stay Connected + a Resident Inquiries form. Listing cards show a price RANGE, bed count, and a "Special offer" flag.

findings.title: Equity Residential's market page is the best large-portfolio finder pattern I found: numbered map pins + neighborhood filter + inline pricing
findings.detail: The homepage is radically minimal — one hero photo, an "Explore +" menu, and a single field: "Where do you want to live?" / "Enter a City, Neighborhood, Zip Code or Property Name". Below it the page is audience-segmented into five blocks: For Our Residents (service request / pay rent, Resident Login, Contact Us) → Work With Us (Career Opportunities) → About Us → Invest With Us (For Investors) → Live With Us (13 market links: New York, Washington DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Boston, Seattle, San Diego, Orange County, Inland Empire, Denver, Austin, Dallas, Atlanta). The /los-angeles page is the payoff: a "Select Neighborhood" filter over a NUMBERED list synced to map pins, where every property carries a neighborhood label as its primary subtitle — Hollywood, Ventura County, Warner Center, Mid-Wilshire, Pasadena, El Segundo, Westside Los Angeles, Westchester, Mar Vista, Playa del Rey, Culver City, Long Beach, Chinatown, Santa Monica, Glendale, Marina Del Rey — plus street address and live per-bedroom pricing inline on the card ("Studio $1,984+ / 1 Bed $2,309+ / 2 Bed $3,459+") or "Coming Soon". Entries without live pricing degrade to "Click Here for Pricing & Availability". Caveat worth flagging: the footer currently reads "©2026 Vivmark Residential" and the LA list mixes Equity properties with Avalon/AVA/eaves-branded ones, so some corporate consolidation appears to have happened; I did not verify the corporate facts and the IA lesson stands regardless.

findings.title: Irvine Company: hamburger-only nav, a named self-guided touring product, and an explicit longevity block
findings.detail: Desktop nav is a hamburger revealing just five items: LOCATIONS (with a drill-down arrow), ABOUT US, OFFERS, SELF-GUIDED TOURING, RESIDENTS — plus a persistent typeahead ("Search by community name, city, or zip"). Homepage: full-bleed hero "Come Home To More" over a named community, then three featured communities with address / "Starting from $3,595" / bed-bath / a paragraph of neighborhood context / "EXPLORE NOW"; then productised benefit blocks — explore TourGuide ("the only mobile app that puts you in control of your homefinding experience by making self-guided touring simple, with Leasing Associates available via live chat"), designed for wellness, exceptional convenience, no better place to work from home, your home team, FOREVER OWNERSHIP ("For over 150 years, Irvine Company has continued to deliver communities with enduring quality…"), smarter homes smoother days; then an editorial block, "Rental Living by Irvine Company". The /locations/los-angeles.html market page carries Price / Beds / Baths / Features filters + a Sort control, a count line ("3 apartment communities in Los Angeles"), SEO neighborhood prose with a READ MORE, a "Cities in Los Angeles" sub-grouping, a full pricing-disclaimer block dated to the day, and a "Join the interest list" form (name, email, phone, desired move-in date, desired floor plan). One central leasing number, 866.371.1063.

findings.title: Greystar: all-in pricing transparency, a Favorites system, and a real neighborhood-guide content layer
findings.detail: Chrome is deliberately thin: Favorites (0) | Business | Contact us + a hamburger. Hero "Apartments made for living" / "Over 1 million apartments to rent — discover yours today" over one search field ("Search by city or Greystar community"). The standout detail: the results module carries an explicit disclosure — "You're seeing Total Monthly Leasing Prices, which include base rent and mandatory monthly costs. Explore each listing for a detailed breakdown." That is an all-in-pricing pattern worth copying. Sections then run: Discover Greystar Communities → Why Rent With Us (Design with you in mind / Places to belong / Always one step ahead) → "Not sure where to look?" city cards with a paragraph of real place copy each (Atlanta, Charlotte Metro, Greater Houston, Los Angeles — "Whether you want an apartment in the San Fernando Valley or Echo Park, LA has something for everyone") plus a "US local guides" entry → "Advice on moving, renting, and more" (When to start looking / How to schedule a tour / Avoiding rental scams) → "A partner you can trust" (B2B). URL-level filtering works (?bedrooms=2&highlight=pets). Footer groups: Homes to rent, Renters' resources, Location guides, Why rent with us, Blog; Business Services, Careers, Regions, Product Specialties.

findings.title: Bozzuto and AvalonBay: minimal chrome over a strong finder, with sub-brands and a state/region directory as the site map
findings.detail: Bozzuto's renter site (/apartments) is a full-bleed interior photograph with only three chrome elements — hamburger, favorites heart, search. Headline "Rent With Us / Love Where You Live", CTA "EXPLORE OUR COMMUNITIES", then a "FIND A COMMUNITY" typeahead with keyboard-navigable results, a featured-community carousel showing starting price + star rating + bed mix + address, a "BOZZUTO LISTENS" feedback block, a "WELCOME HOME COMMITMENT" ("a checklist of 70 items and a 30-day guarantee"), a top-rated-reputation block, then an "Explore Our Properties" A-Z state directory (22 states) as the footer site map. Corporate nav spans Rent With Us / Careers / Contact Us / Our Companies (Property Management, Construction, Development, Wye River Insurance) / About Bozzuto (Belonging & Impact, Bozzuto Experience, Corporate Social Responsibility, Leadership, News & Press, Our Work). AvalonBay's nav is Locations | About Us | Careers | Investors | Residents | Create Account / Login, and its homepage is organised by SUB-BRAND (AVA, Avalon, Eaves by Avalon, Kanso, Furnished+) then by named resident programs (WAG Pet Program, FIT Wellness, Bilt Rewards, Technology Package, Digital Resident Services, Relocation Advantage), with region-based browsing by state.

findings.title: Related Rentals and Camden: city → neighborhood → building hierarchy, and 'Investors' promoted into the primary nav
findings.detail: Related Rentals nav: Choose City | Our Buildings | Search All Apartments | Related Life | Furnished Apartments | Blog | Contact Agent. Hero "Expect More at Home" with a four-part filter (city, neighborhood/building, bedrooms, monthly rent range). Buildings are browsed as a strict hierarchy — city → neighborhood → building — with a Property dropdown listing 50+ buildings; dropdown-driven, not map-driven. "Our Locations" is seven city cards each with a named Featured Building (NYC/One Hudson Yards, Boston/The Arlington, Chicago/One Bennett Park, Los Angeles/Argyle House, SF/Mason On Mariposa, DC/10K, West Palm Beach). "The Related Life" is the resident-services brand: 24/7 concierge, move-in coordination, package delivery, pet care, wellness and fitness partnerships. Camden puts Investors in the PRIMARY nav — Home | About | Blog | Careers | Investors | Find An Apartment | Log In | Comparison List — and offers a side-by-side unit Comparison List, a MyCamden portal, and resident testimonial + blog carousels covering local attractions. Both show that a portfolio operator can foreground investor material without wrecking the renter path.

findings.title: Decron is the best LA template for legacy storytelling: a named human founder plus a hard-numbers proof bar
findings.detail: Decron (Los Angeles, founded 1950s) nav: Communities | Company | Culture | Careers | Contact | Login. Hero: "Strong Foundation, enduring spirit" with a single CTA, "SEARCH APARTMENTS". The homepage is a sequence of legacy-framed statements, each linking deeper: "A Legacy of Growth through joy" → Our Story; "A Vision to Create lasting value" → Our Company; "More than Just diversity & inclusion" → Our Culture; "Investing in People, not just properties" → Careers; "A Legacy of Leading with integrity & responsibility"; "Committed to Growth, one opportunity at a time"; "The Gift of Philanthropy"; "Find A Community where we are now". The /company page anchors everything on a named person — founder Jack Nagel, "immigrant and Holocaust survivor", who built a single development in the 1950s that became a multibillion-dollar enterprise, with "irrepressible optimism" as a stated cultural inheritance — and backs it with a stats bar: 60+ years, 3 states, 300+ employees, 10,000+ apartment units, 1 million sq ft retail & office, $200+ million invested in capital improvements. That last stat (capital reinvested) is the single most persuasive number an owner-operator can publish, because it proves stewardship rather than acquisition.

findings.title: Goldrich Kest ('Welcoming You Since 1957') shows the legacy-plus-stats pattern working for a family firm at Wiseman's scale
findings.detail: GK Management / Goldrich Kest is a Culver City family firm founded 1957 by Jona Goldrich and Sol Kest. Nav is deliberately short: Our Portfolio | Careers | Our Story | Contact — with Founders as a sub-item under Our Story. Hero is a property carousel under the tagline "Welcoming You Since 1957". Homepage order: four portfolio-category cards (Luxury Living, Senior & Affordable Living, Marina Living, Commercial/Retail) → "A Legacy of Connection" (company history and founders) → "Strategic Locations in California & Beyond" → a property showcase grid (The Highland, Museum Tower, Corazon, Milagro, Museum Terrace) → a stats bar (65+ years experience, 200+ properties, 500+ team members, 7 awards) → "Join the GK Family" careers section with employee testimonials → "See What's New at GK" news. Two lessons for Wiseman: (a) segmenting the portfolio by TYPE as the top-level entry works when you have a lot of properties, and (b) a family firm can lead with the founders' names without it feeling self-indulgent, because the stats bar immediately converts the story into credibility.

findings.title: G.H. Palmer is the cautionary tale: a large LA family portfolio reduced to a splash page and disconnected microsites
findings.detail: G.H. Palmer Associates (Beverly Hills, one of LA's best-known family apartment developers) still serves a gateway/splash page whose only action is "Click Here to Enter". Behind it is a bare grid of five communities — The Piero, The Orsini, Lorenzo, The Visconti, The Medici — each linking OUT to its own separate website. There is no portfolio nav, no About/History, no Careers, no resident services, no search or filter; the footer carries only a Beverly Hills address, a phone number, an email, and a Corporate Login. This is structurally the same failure mode Wiseman has today (a thin hub that dumps users into disconnected per-property sites), just without the RentCafe listing layer. It is the concrete argument for consolidating rather than proliferating: a portfolio operator that only links out never accrues brand or SEO equity at the parent level.

findings.title: Sentral: audience-segmented navigation with explanatory sublines, a dual-CTA hero, and an explicit 'For Owners & Developers' block
findings.detail: Sentral (36 communities across 20 cities, incl. The Park in Santa Monica and Respara Brentwood in LA) has the cleanest audience-segmented nav I found. The slide-out menu has exactly three destinations, each with a one-line descriptor: STAY WITH US — "Furnished stays, 1 night to a whole summer"; LIVE WITH US — "Apartment living, residentially priced"; PARTNER WITH US — "Institutional-grade property management". Hero: "Live with soul. / Stay with energy. / Love where you are, with Sentral." over a tabbed booking widget with TWO modes — BOOK A STAY (Where / Check-in / Check-out / CHECK RATES) and LEASE AN APARTMENT. Homepage runs: the dual-mode explainer ("Book it like a hotel. Live or stay in it like a home.") → "The Sentral Difference" with four numbered experience pillars, each illustrated by a NAMED property and city (01 Private member clubs / Quincy, San Francisco; 02 Food & beverage / Maman at Sentral Wynwood, Miami; 03 Events & programming / Miro, San Jose; 04 Health & wellness / The Park, Santa Monica) → a twelve-city grid → "Live with us / FIND YOUR HOME" featured leases → a resident travel benefit → a rewards program → "FOR OWNERS & DEVELOPERS — We change the math on your asset" with a PARTNER WITH US CTA. That last block is the model for Wiseman's development/owner-operator side living on the same site as the renter side without competing with it.

findings.title: ila (ila.rent) shows how far a rental COLLECTION brand can strip its navigation when the finder and the perks do the work
findings.detail: ila is a UK build-to-rent collection and a 2025 Hermes gold winner for website design. Its entire persistent nav is two links — home and Contact — plus one "Search by location…" field. Everything else is scroll: a bold stacked-type hero ("Rent / more than / just a home" — "Top-tier amenities, local perks, resident events and friendly on-site teams — all included") → a Featured homes carousel where each card is just CITY + BUILDING NAME (London/ALPERTON DEPOT, Cardiff/ANCHOR WORKS, London/KEW CURVE, Salford/OLDFIELD WHARF) → "INTERIOR DESIGNED SPACES / Be proud of where you live" → an amenity ticker → a six-tile perks grid stated as promises, not features (DEDICATED TEAM, PAINTED WALLS — "we've partnered with COAT Paints so that you can customise your apartment", PET FRIENDLY, MAINTENANCE SUPPORT, EASY IN-APP ADMIN, EVENTS & OFFERS) → a resident-events block → "Exclusive resident offers" with named local and national brand partnerships (The Box Co., COAT Paints, The Gym Group). The transferable idea for a 45-year LA operator: the differentiator is expressed as concrete, ownable promises and real local partnerships, not adjectives.

findings.title: Kasa and the hospitality-adjacent brands lead with local guides and a visible partner track
findings.detail: Kasa's nav is four items — Travel | Company | Get help | My bookings — over a date-driven search (location, check-in/check-out, guests). Homepage sections run: "The Kasa experience" (virtual check-in, Wi-Fi, pet-friendly, 24/7 support, quality bedding) → "Flexible spaces for every trip" (long-term stays, groups, corporate partnerships, corporate housing) → "Find your next destination" / browse all locations → a featured-property carousel → guest testimonials → "Hospitality at your fingertips" (easy booking, virtual front desk, safe arrival/departure) → "Explore local guides" (Miami, Los Angeles, Traverse City) → help centre. There is a distinct partner track — Multifamily partners, Hotel partners, Mint House, cleaning partner resources. The two patterns worth stealing: (a) an editorial local-guides layer used as an SEO and trust asset, and (b) a separate, clearly signposted B2B/partner path that never intrudes on the consumer flow.

findings.title: Investment-manager sites (Cityview, CGI+, Carmel Partners) prove the opposite failure mode — an investor-first IA that abandons the renter
findings.detail: Cityview (LA, founded 2003): nav WHO WE ARE | INVESTMENT STRATEGIES | PORTFOLIO | PEOPLE | PRESS | CONTACT | LOGIN (→ cityview.investorcafe.app). Hero: "We transform Cities into Communities, People into Neighbors, and Houses into Homes." The /portfolio page is a grid of twelve "Featured Projects" with city labels and "Sold" badges and a disclaimer that it is "a representative sample" — it is a track record for LPs, not a finder; there is no way for a renter to reach a lease. CGI+ (founded 2013 by Gidi Cohen): The Company | Our Approach | Investments | Investors | Contact Us, with six core values and an investor-portal login. Carmel Partners: The Firm | Projects | ESG+R | Careers | Contact, hero "Properties that impress. Expertise that inspires." Sares Regis: About Us | SRG Residential | SRG Commercial | Careers | News | Contact — and its homepage still carries a COVID-19 Updates block, a clear staleness signal. Because Wiseman is simultaneously owner, developer and manager, the site must carry BOTH audiences; these sites show what happens if the capital-markets voice wins.

findings.title: The standard information architecture for a portfolio operator of this size, derived from what every credible peer actually has
findings.detail: Across Essex, AvalonBay, Camden, Bozzuto, Greystar, Irvine, Decron, Goldrich Kest, Moss and Douglas Emmett, the same five blocks recur in the same order. (1) FINDER — one search entry point in the header on every page, always a single typeahead accepting city, neighborhood, zip, or property name (Essex, Greystar, Bozzuto, Equity, Irvine all use exactly this). (2) PORTFOLIO HIERARCHY — market/region → neighborhood → property, with real landing pages at the neighborhood tier (Essex's nine metro chips, Equity's 13 markets with a Select Neighborhood filter, Related's city→neighborhood→building, Moss's six LA areas, Douglas Emmett's footer grouping). (3) RESIDENTS — a content page distinct from the portal login, covering pay rent, maintenance requests, FAQs, perks, and a contact route (Essex /current-resident is the cleanest example; Related brands it "Related Life"; Camden brands it MyCamden). (4) COMPANY — About/Our Story, History, Leadership, News, and for owner-operators a Development or Management Services section (Moss, Decron, Goldrich Kest, Douglas Emmett all split these). (5) CAREERS — always its own top-level item at this size (Essex, AvalonBay, Camden, Bozzuto, Decron, Goldrich Kest, Moss, Sares Regis, Carmel). A sixth, INVESTORS/OWNERS, appears when relevant and is either top-level (Camden, AvalonBay, Essex, Douglas Emmett) or folded into a 'Partner With Us' block (Sentral, Kasa). Footer is universally used as the full site map, with the entire portfolio enumerated by geography for SEO.

findings.title: What separates top-tier from template sites: named places, live inventory on the card, one identity, and editorial substance
findings.detail: Four differences held consistently. (1) NAMED PLACES, NOT JUST ADDRESSES. Top-tier cards lead with the neighborhood (Equity's LA page tags every property Hollywood / Mar Vista / Culver City / Mid-Wilshire); template sites show a street address and a zip. (2) LIVE INVENTORY ON THE CARD. Equity shows per-bedroom pricing inline; Irvine shows "Starting from $3,595" plus a dated disclaimer; Bozzuto shows starting price plus a 4.7 star rating; Greystar shows an all-in total monthly price with a disclosure. Wiseman's cards show a single price and a phone number. (3) ONE IDENTITY. Bozzuto, Greystar, Essex and Equity keep the renter inside one domain and one design system all the way to the floor plan; Wiseman, G.H. Palmer and Goldrich Kest bounce users to per-property sites. (4) EDITORIAL SUBSTANCE. Greystar's local guides and renting advice, Irvine's Rental Living, Camden's neighborhood blog, Kasa's city guides, Presidio's History page — all give the parent brand something to rank for and something to say. Template sites substitute a welcome paragraph and a photo slider, which is exactly Wiseman's current homepage. A fifth, emerging in 2026: transparent all-in pricing (Greystar) and self-guided/virtual touring as a named product (Irvine's TourGuide).

findings.title: What a 72-property finder needs that a single-property site does not — concretely
findings.detail: Wiseman's current finder paginates 25 of 72 with an unstyled pin map and no neighborhood facet; the only grouping signal is a category tag on some cards ('APARTMENT, WEST LA', 'APARTMENT, CONDO, WEST LA'), applied inconsistently. What the peer set proves is required at this count: (a) a NEIGHBORHOOD FACET as the first filter, not price — Equity's "Select Neighborhood", Essex's nine metro chips, Moss's six LA areas; Wiseman's own footprint gives ready-made facets (West LA, Brentwood, Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City, Hollywood/Beverly Grove, Glendale). (b) SYNCED MAP + LIST with numbered pins so pin 17 is row 17 (Equity does exactly this; Essex offers a Map only / List only toggle). (c) FILTERS THAT MATTER FOR A MIXED-VINTAGE PORTFOLIO — beds, baths, price, move-in date, pets, parking, in-unit laundry, and building type; Presidio proves you can smuggle era and typology into RentCafe's property-type taxonomy ('POST WWII', 'HISTORIC', 'DUPLEX/TRIPLEX'), which for a 45-year LA portfolio is a genuine differentiator (a 1970s courtyard building versus a 2026 new-build are different products). (d) LIVE AVAILABILITY AND A 'COMING SOON' STATE so a 72-property portfolio never looks empty (Presidio's "Coming Soon! 746-A Three-Bedroom historic duplex home!"). (e) A FAVORITES/COMPARE LIST, because at 72 properties renters shortlist — Greystar puts Favorites (0) in the header, Camden has a Comparison List, Bozzuto has a heart icon, and Wiseman already has a Favorites tab buried in the search page. (f) NEIGHBORHOOD LANDING PAGES that rank independently and funnel into the filtered finder. (g) AN INTEREST LIST / WAITLIST FORM for when nothing matches — Irvine captures bedrooms, price range and desired move-in date; Presidio has a "Housing Interest Form". (h) ONE CENTRAL LEASING NUMBER as the fallback (Irvine 866.371.1063, Presidio 844-808-6177) rather than eight per-property numbers.

findings.title: The five conversion paths peers actually build, and their relative prominence
findings.detail: Observed consistently across the set, in priority order. (1) FIND/FILTER → PROPERTY — always the hero action, always a single field. (2) SCHEDULE A TOUR — increasingly a named product rather than a form: Irvine has SELF-GUIDED TOURING as a top-level nav item and "TourGuide" as a branded app with live leasing-associate chat; Greystar runs a "How to schedule a tour" advice page. Wiseman currently offers only "In-person and virtual tours available by appointment" in prose on the Motor Tides block, with a phone number. (3) APPLY — Wiseman already has this wired (RentCafe onlineleasing guestlogin) but it is a per-card "APPLY NOW" that opens a new window with no context. (4) RESIDENT LOGIN / PAY RENT / MAINTENANCE — everyone puts the login in the header utility bar, but the good ones ALSO have a resident content page behind it (Essex /current-resident with Pay Rent, Maintenance Requests, FAQs, Perks). Wiseman has the login and nothing behind it. (5) CONTACT LEASING — the good ones route by intent and capture preferences; Irvine's form takes bedrooms, price range, move-in date and free text, Presidio has a separate "Housing Interest Form". Two secondary paths matter for Wiseman specifically because it is also a developer and manager: PARTNER/OWNER INQUIRY (Sentral's "FOR OWNERS & DEVELOPERS", Moss's "Due Diligence / Proposals", Kasa's Multifamily partners) and CAREERS APPLY.

findings.title: The playbook for a company whose differentiator is longevity and local roots rather than scale or luxury
findings.detail: Six moves, each verified on a real site. (1) NAME A HUMAN. Decron anchors on Jack Nagel, immigrant and Holocaust survivor, first development in the 1950s; Goldrich Kest names Jona Goldrich and Sol Kest with a dedicated /founders page. Abstract 'family-owned' language loses to a named person with a real story. (2) PUT THE YEAR IN THE LOCKUP. "Welcoming You Since 1957" (Goldrich Kest); "PROFESSIONALLY MANAGED REAL ESTATE SINCE 1960!" (Moss). (3) CONVERT THE STORY TO NUMBERS IMMEDIATELY. Decron: 60+ years / 3 states / 300+ employees / 10,000+ units / 1M sq ft / $200M+ invested in capital improvements. Goldrich Kest: 65+ years / 200+ properties / 500+ team members. Irvine: "For over 150 years" under a heading literally called "forever ownership". The capital-reinvestment number is the one that proves stewardship rather than mere tenure. (4) MAKE THE PLACE THE PRODUCT. Presidio's homepage is a numbered map of 25 named neighborhoods and its History page is organised by architectural era; Moss leads its homepage with a six-area NEIGHBORHOODS row and a dusk LA skyline captioned "IT'S PERSONAL". A 45-year operator should be able to say things about Brentwood and Venice that a national REIT cannot. (5) SHOW THE BUILDINGS AS ARTEFACTS. Presidio tags listings 'HISTORIC' and 'POST WWII' and writes about a Victorian built in 1889; Veritas presents its portfolio as per-building historical narratives with photo galleries rather than a spec grid. (6) PROMISE SERVICE IN CONCRETE, CHECKABLE TERMS. Bozzuto publishes "a checklist of 70 items and a 30-day guarantee"; ila publishes six named resident promises. Wiseman's homepage currently says management should be "professional, communicative, and proactive" — three adjectives with nothing testable behind them.

summary:
Two things make this build unusual. First, the renter-facing UX bar is well documented and Wiseman's current data model cannot meet it: the portfolio file at `/Users/wangzhen/Documents/wiseman website/corporate/data/properties.psv` has 72 rows with only ten columns (name, category, beds, baths, sqft, address, price, phone, path, image). It carries no pets, parking, in-unit laundry, availability date, year built, unit-level inventory, or lat/long — which are precisely the filters renters use. 18 of 72 properties have no neighborhood tag at all (8 of the 13 Brentwood-ZIP 90049 properties among them), which blocks both neighborhood filtering and the neighborhood landing pages that drive local SEO. Meanwhile the actual listings live on a separate RentCafe subdomain (properties.wisemanresidential.com), splitting authority away from the root domain. Fixing the data model and consolidating listings onto the primary domain are prerequisites, not enhancements.

Second, the compliance picture is genuinely in flux and most of what you'll find online about it right now is wrong. HUD withdrew eight Fair Housing & Equal Opportunity guidance documents — including the April 2024 digital-platform advertising guidance — via a Federal Register notice published April 6, 2026, effective September 17, 2025. That does NOT reduce exposure here: the operative prohibition is the statute itself (42 U.S.C. 3604(c)) and 24 CFR 100.75, both untouched, and California's FEHA (Gov. Code 12955) is broader than federal law and entirely unaffected. Separately, I found that multiple industry blogs claim California now requires all mandatory fees to be baked into advertised rent (variously citing "SB 611" and "AB 747"). Both claims are false: leginfo confirms SB 611 (chaptered 9/19/2024) covers notice fees, check-payment fees and deposit caps with no advertising provision, and AB 747 (Chapter 563, 2025) is the SPARE Act on service of process. The actual advertising/fee-disclosure bill is AB 1248 (Haney), which was held in suspense in 2025 and is not law. Build to a fee-transparency design because it's good practice and AB 1248 may return, but do not represent it as a current legal requirement.
recommendations: Extend the property schema before building UI. Add to properties.psv (or migrate to JSON/SQLite): beds_min, beds_max, baths_min, baths_max, rent_min, rent_max as integers; available_date; neighborhood as a controlled vocabulary; property_type split out of the category field; lat, lng (geocoded once and persisted); jurisdiction; and booleans for pets_cats, pets_dogs, parking, in_unit_laundry, ac, elevator, controlled_access, accessible_units. The current ten columns cannot support the filter set renters expect.

Backfill the 18 untagged neighborhoods by ZIP, prioritizing the 8 properties in 90049 that should read Brentwood. Until that is done, neighborhood filtering and neighborhood landing pages — the highest-value SEO assets — are structurally impossible.

Ship these filters, in this order of priority: neighborhood, beds, price range, availability date, pets, in-unit laundry, parking, baths. Encode filter state in the URL so results are shareable and the back button works.
Build a synced map + list view, but make the list the accessible primary. Every pin needs a corresponding focusable list item; the list must be complete and usable with the map fully disabled.

Add a comparison tray (pin 2–4 properties, side-by-side) and saved favorites that work via localStorage without requiring an account. 77% of RentCafe respondents found comparison helpful in narrowing their search.

Put the Equal Housing Opportunity logo and wordmark in the global footer of every page, sized no smaller than the Wiseman logo, as a real with alt="Equal Housing Opportunity" — plus on every property detail page and every downloadable PDF.
Put the responsible broker's DRE-registered entity name and 8-digit license number in the global footer. Confirm the licensed entity with Wiseman first — do not assume it is 'Wiseman Residential'.

Build to WCAG 2.1 Level AA in code. Do not install an accessibility overlay widget; UsableNet counted 99 lawsuits in June 2025 alone against defendants using them. Test the search, filter, map and contact-form flows with keyboard only and with a screen reader, since property search is the barrier most often named in demand letters.

Run every line of listing and neighborhood copy through a fair-housing review against the California protected-class list, which is broader than the federal one. Neighborhood pages are the highest-risk surface — restrict them to verifiable non-demographic facts (transit, distances, named businesses, walk times).

Audit the photo library in aggregate for human-model representation across all 72 properties, not shot by shot. A pattern showing only young childless adults is the documented risk, not any single image.

Never publish 'No Section 8' or equivalent, and audit non-copy surfaces too: income-requirement badges, minimum-income calculators, contact-form qualifier dropdowns, and any leasing-chatbot pre-qualification logic. Source of income is a FEHA protected class under SB 329.

Design the pricing display all-in-ready — advertised rent plus a clearly itemized 'other monthly charges' block — but tell the client this is good practice and AB 1248 preparedness, NOT a current legal requirement. Correct the record if anyone cites SB 611 or AB 747 for this.

Add a Residents → Your Rights & Resources hub linking LAHD's official RSO, Renter Protections Notice and Right to Counsel pages, with plain-language explanation and an explicit statement that unit-specific disclosures come with the lease. Do not reproduce the notices themselves as if the site were the delivery mechanism.

Store a jurisdiction field per property and scope any rent-control or tenant-rights content per property. Broadway Glendale is outside the LA RSO entirely, and Alfred Atlas in ZIP 90069 sits near the West Hollywood boundary and should be confirmed.

Give the resident stack five one-click destinations from the primary nav: Pay Rent, Maintenance Request (with a separate always-visible 24/7 emergency phone path), Residents hub (move-in guide, utilities setup with real LADWP/SoCalGas links, renters insurance, parking/package/access policies), Rights & Resources, and per-property contact.

Serve property detail pages from the primary domain at /apartments/{neighborhood}/{property-slug}/ rather than the RentCafe subdomain, using the RentCafe/SecureCAFE handoff only at the Apply step — the pattern already used for Motor Tides.

Implement layered JSON-LD: Organization site-wide (foundingDate 1980, sameAs to Yelp/Google), ApartmentComplex per property with geo and amenityFeature, and nested Apartment + Offer per floor plan with price, availability and availabilityStarts. Validate at validator.schema.org and match the NAP to Google Business Profile exactly.
Build five neighborhood landing pages (Brentwood, West LA/Sawtelle, Hollywood, Venice, Palms) that list their properties and interlink from every property in that neighborhood.

Surface trust signals a REIT can't copy: founded 1980 by Isaac Cohanzad, 45 years in LA, vertically integrated, named leadership with photos, real corporate address with hours, aggregate review ratings linked out to Yelp and Google, and published leasing/maintenance response times you can actually hold to.

If the portfolio includes TOC-derived covenanted affordable units, state so plainly with an inquiry path. Concealing income-restricted inventory creates fair-housing exposure; surfacing it is both compliant and differentiating.
Add a Spanish toggle for search, property detail, contact and the residents hub with correct lang attributes — and never machine-translate legal or disclosure text.

Manually audit the live site in a browser for current EHO logo, accessibility statement, and DRE disclosure. Both wisemanresidential.com and properties.wisemanresidential.com are behind Cloudflare and returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so I could not verify what is currently there.
donots: Do not claim California currently requires all mandatory fees to be included in advertised rent. leginfo confirms SB 611 (chaptered 9/19/2024) covers notice fees, check-payment fees and deposit caps with no advertising provision, and AB 747 (Chapter 563, 2025) is the SPARE Act on service of process. AB 1248 is the real advertising bill and it was held in suspense in 2025.

Do not cite HUD's April 29, 2024 digital-platform advertising guidance as current authority. It was withdrawn effective September 17, 2025 per the Federal Register notice published April 6, 2026. Cite 42 U.S.C. 3604(c) and 24 CFR 100.75 instead, which are unchanged.

Do not tell the client the DOJ April 2024 WCAG 2.1 AA rule legally binds them. That rule is ADA Title II and applies only to state and local government entities. WCAG 2.1 AA is the right build target for other reasons.
Do not install a third-party accessibility overlay widget and represent it as compliance. It measurably increases litigation risk.
Do not publish 'No Section 8', voucher-exclusion language, or pre-qualification logic that ignores the subsidy portion of income — unlawful under FEHA per SB 329.

Do not write listing or neighborhood copy that describes the imagined resident ('perfect for young professionals', 'ideal for singles', 'great for empty nesters') or characterizes an area in demographic terms.

Do not reproduce the LAHD Notice of Renters' Protections, RSO registration certificate, or Right to Counsel notice on the website as though the site satisfies the delivery obligation. These are served and posted at the property.

Do not state one rent-control rule set portfolio-wide. Broadway Glendale in Glendale is outside the LA RSO, and AB 1482 exemption claims require specific statutory notice language delivered with the lease.
Do not fabricate, selectively excerpt, or average review scores. Pull them live or cite source and date.

Do not invent amenity, pet, parking or laundry data to populate the new filters. Those fields do not exist in properties.psv today and must be sourced from Wiseman, not inferred from photos or property names.
Do not geocode addresses at runtime. Persist lat/lng in the data file.
Do not require account creation before a visitor can browse, filter, or save a favorite.
Do not treat the map as the only path to inventory — it is not an accessible primary interface.
Do not claim to have audited the current live wisemanresidential.com. Both domains returned HTTP 403 behind Cloudflare and were not inspected.

findings.title: Renters filter on attributes the current data model doesn't contain
findings.detail: The portfolio source file has exactly ten fields: name|category|beds|baths|sqft|address|price|phone|path|image. Beds and baths are stored as human-readable ranges ("Studio-5 Beds", "1-5 Baths") and price as a string range ("$3,945.00 to $5,595.00"), so neither is machine-filterable without parsing into numeric min/max columns. There is no field for pets, parking, in-unit laundry, availability date, year built, air conditioning, accessibility features, or geo-coordinates. NMHC/Grace Hill data consistently shows pet friendliness and property security among the top leasing-decision factors, and in-unit laundry and parking are standard filter primitives on every competing portal. Before any UI work, the schema needs: beds_min/beds_max, baths_min/baths_max, rent_min/rent_max (integers), available_date, neighborhood (controlled vocabulary), lat, lng, plus booleans for pets_cats, pets_dogs, parking, in_unit_laundry, ac, elevator, controlled_access, accessible_units. Also add jurisdiction and rso_status as data fields even if not displayed publicly — they drive which disclosures and resources the property page should surface.

findings.title: 18 of 72 properties carry no neighborhood tag, which blocks the highest-value SEO pages
findings.detail: Counting the `category` column: 23 "Apartment, West LA", 23 "Apartment, Hollywood", 6 "Apartment, Brentwood", 1 "Apartment, Culver City", 1 "Apartment, Condo, West LA", and 18 bare "Apartment" with no neighborhood. The untagged 18 break down by ZIP as: 8 in 90049, 3 in 90048, 2 in 90291, and one each in 91205, 90064, 90046, 90034, 90025. That means 13 properties sit in ZIP 90049 (Brentwood) but only 6 are tagged Brentwood — the single most premium neighborhood in the portfolio is more than half invisible to any neighborhood filter or landing page. Neighborhood is also doing double duty as a product category in this field ("Apartment, Condo, West LA"), which is a schema smell: property_type and neighborhood should be separate columns. ZIP codes are present in every address and map cleanly to neighborhoods (90025 West LA/Sawtelle, 90049 Brentwood, 90048 Beverly Grove, 90046/90038 Hollywood, 90034 Palms, 90291 Venice, 90064 Rancho Park), so this is mechanically fixable.

findings.title: Listings live on a RentCafe subdomain, splitting SEO authority from the root domain
findings.detail: Search results surface both wisemanresidential.com and properties.wisemanresidential.com as separate RentCafe-branded entities (page titles literally read "| Apartments in Los Angeles, CA | RENTCafe"). Google treats subdomains as substantially separate sites for authority purposes, so every inbound link and brand mention to the root domain does little for the pages that actually convert. The revamp should serve property detail pages from the primary domain under a stable path convention — /apartments/{neighborhood}/{property-slug}/ — with the RentCafe/SecureCAFE flow used only for the application handoff (the Motor Tides pattern in redesign/CONTENT.md already does this, linking out to a securecafe.com guestlogin URL for Apply). Note that both root domains are behind Cloudflare and returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so I could not verify the live site's current markup, footer, EHO logo, or accessibility statement — someone should audit those manually in a browser.

findings.title: Photos beat every other media type; virtual tours are secondary and floor-plan-level beats amenity-level
findings.detail: A RentCafe survey fielded Jan 3–Feb 1 2024 with 10,110 respondents (8,446 US) found 73% of renters prioritize interior apartment photos when searching, and that individual floor-plan virtual tours are valued well above community-amenity virtual tours. Zillow's Consumer Housing Trends data puts 3D/virtual tours at 27% and recorded video tours at 22% considered essential, versus 50% for photos and 40% for floor plans — but 57% consider at least one digital media feature essential, and 62% of Gen Z say 3D tours give a better feel for space than static photos. The practical ordering for the build: abundant interior photography per floor plan first, dimensioned floor plan images second, per-floor-plan 3D tours third, amenity video last. Critically, Zillow found 59% of recent renters said seeing lease terms, rent amount and fees was essential — a higher bar than any visual feature. Pricing and terms transparency outranks media.

findings.title: Comparison and reviews are decisive, and reviews are the strongest trust signal in the category
findings.detail: RentCafe reports 77% of renters found property comparison helpful in narrowing their search — a direct argument for a build-in compare tray (pin 2–4 properties, side-by-side on beds/baths/rent/neighborhood/pets/parking/laundry/availability). On reviews, the 2022 NMHC/Grace Hill Renter Preferences Survey found 69% of renters referenced ratings and reviews in their most recent search, 84% said review content influenced their leasing decision, and 79% said reviews stopped them from visiting specific properties. Other industry survey data puts 98% saying reviews matter to the decision and 55% requiring at least four ratings before considering a property. Wiseman has substantial existing review inventory — 568 Yelp reviews and 91 VeryApt reviews at 6.8 — so the site should surface aggregate ratings and link out rather than hide them. Do not fabricate or selectively excerpt; pull live or cite the source and date.

findings.title: HUD withdrew eight fair housing guidance documents effective Sept 17, 2025 — but the operative law is unchanged
findings.detail: A Federal Register notice published April 6, 2026 (doc 2026-06624) withdrew eight FHEO guidance documents effective September 17, 2025, under Executive Orders 14192 and 14219. The withdrawn list includes: the April 29 2024 guidance on applying the FHA to advertising through digital platforms; FHEO 2020-01 on assistance animals; FHEO Notice 2013-01 on service/assistance animals; the Feb 2024 source-of-income testing memorandum; the 2021 special purpose credit programs statement; the 2007 Title VI limited-English-proficiency guidance; the 2021 EO 13988 implementation; and the 2022 criminal-records guidance. What this does NOT change: 42 U.S.C. 3604(c) and 24 CFR 100.75 remain fully in force. 100.75 makes it unlawful to make, print or publish any notice, statement or advertisement indicating a preference, limitation or discrimination based on a protected class, and expressly reaches "words, phrases, photographs, symbols or forms," selective use of advertising media, and expressions of preference to agents or prospects. Build to the statute, not to the withdrawn guidance. Note HUD's May 2 2024 tenant-screening guidance does not appear on the withdrawal list, though I could not independently confirm its current status.

findings.title: The Equal Housing Opportunity logo is 'should' not 'must' federally — but treat it as mandatory anyway
findings.detail: The EHO logo/statement requirement came from 24 CFR Part 109, which was withdrawn from the CFR by directive FR-4029-F-01 effective May 1, 1996. HUD nonetheless continues to treat Part 109 as describing the matters it reviews when evaluating advertising compliance and investigating complaints. Part 109's sizing rule: the EHO logo should be at least equal in size to the largest other logotype on the piece; where no other logo appears, bold display type clearly visible; in space advertising under 4 column inches, the slogan is used instead. The practical build standard: EHO logo plus the words "Equal Housing Opportunity" in the global footer on every page, sized no smaller than the Wiseman logo mark, with real alt text (alt="Equal Housing Opportunity"), not a background image and not an icon font. Also include it on every property detail page and in any downloadable PDF flyer or floor plate.

findings.title: Listing copy: describe the unit, never the imagined occupant
findings.detail: The legal test under 3604(c)/100.75 is whether copy indicates a preference, limitation or discrimination as to a protected class. The reliable editorial rule is: describe the property, not the person you picture living in it. Concretely risky in apartment copy — familial status: "perfect for young professionals," "ideal for singles," "perfect for empty nesters," "adult building," "no children," "mature residents," "quiet building" when used to screen families, and bedroom-count occupancy statements framed as preferences. Disability: "must be able to climb stairs," "not suitable for wheelchairs," "able-bodied." Religion/national origin/race: naming churches, temples or ethnic enclaves as selling points, or "exclusive," "restricted," "private," "integrated." California adds protected classes federal law lacks — including source of income, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, marital status, ancestry, genetic information, veteran/military status, and immigration status — so California copy review is strictly broader than federal. Neighborhood pages are the highest-risk surface on a portfolio site: describing an area's "character" or "vibe" in demographic terms is textbook steering. Keep neighborhood copy to verifiable, non-demographic facts — transit lines, distances, named businesses, parks, walk times.

findings.title: Photography and human models carry their own fair housing rule
findings.detail: Part 109's human-models guidance — still HUD's stated review framework — holds that models in photographs, drawings or graphics may not be used to indicate exclusiveness by protected class, and should indicate the housing is open to all. Models should reasonably represent majority and minority groups in the metropolitan area, both sexes, and where appropriate families with children. It also warns specifically against selective use: running models primarily in media serving one racial or national-origin segment without a complementary campaign directed at others. For an LA Westside portfolio this matters concretely — lifestyle photography that shows only young childless adults across 72 properties is a documented pattern, not an aesthetic choice, and it is discoverable. Audit the image library in aggregate, not shot by shot.

findings.title: Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA is the real target, and overlay widgets increase risk rather than reduce it
findings.detail: Two independent legal hooks reach an apartment operator's website. (1) ADA Title III: DOJ's Title III Technical Assistance Manual treats a private residential complex's rental/leasing office as a place of public accommodation, and courts applying the nexus theory extend that to the website that serves it. (2) The FHA independently prohibits disability discrimination in nearly all rental transactions, including making dwellings unavailable — which reaches an inaccessible search/apply flow directly, and unlike Title III has no 'physical place' limitation. Important precision: DOJ's April 2024 final rule adopting WCAG 2.1 Level AA applies only to state and local government entities under Title II, not to private landlords; its compliance dates were extended by an interim final rule to April 26 2027 (large entities) and April 26 2028 (small entities/special districts). It does not bind Wiseman, but WCAG 2.1 AA is the standard DOJ references and the one plaintiffs plead, so it is the correct build target. Real estate and property management saw a marked rise in web accessibility demand letters in 2024–2025 with property search functionality cited as the primary barrier. Critically, UsableNet counted 99 new lawsuits in June 2025 alone against defendants using third-party accessibility overlay widgets — do not install AccessiBe/UserWay-style overlays and treat the problem as solved; remediate in code.

findings.title: Source-of-income protection makes 'No Section 8' language illegal in California — including in filters and forms
findings.detail: SB 329 (signed Oct 8 2019, effective Jan 1 2020) amended FEHA to include housing subsidies within "source of income" under Gov. Code 12955. Section 12955 defines source of income to include lawful verifiable income paid to a tenant or paid to a landlord on the tenant's behalf, expressly including federal Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers. FEHA makes it unlawful to make, print or publish any notice, statement or advertisement indicating a preference, limitation or discrimination based on any protected class including source of income, so "No Section 8" or "We do not participate in Section 8" is unlawful advertising. For the site build this is not just a copy rule: it reaches a minimum-income calculator or 'income requirement: 3x rent' badge applied without accounting for the voucher portion, a contact form dropdown that asks about voucher status as a qualifier, and any pre-qualification logic in a leasing chatbot. Wiseman's TOC-derived affordable set-aside units make this doubly live — those units interact with subsidy programs by design.

findings.title: California DRE license number belongs in the site footer
findings.detail: Under Bus. & Prof. Code 10130 and 10131(b), anyone who for compensation leases or rents real property for others, solicits tenants, or collects rent must hold a DRE broker license or operate under one. There is no separate 'property management' license in California — the broker license covers it. B&P Code 10140.6, implemented by Commissioner's Regulation 10 CCR 2770.1 (with 2773 on format), requires licensees to disclose their license number on solicitation materials intended to be the first point of contact with consumers — the enumerated examples include business cards, stationery, flyers, and print and electronic media advertisements. A corporate marketing website that generates leasing inquiries is squarely first-point-of-contact material. Practical build rule: put the responsible broker's exact DRE-registered entity name and 8-digit license number (leading zeros included) in the global footer, in type no smaller than the smallest type used elsewhere in the footer. You'll need Wiseman to confirm the licensed entity — note the BBB record lists 'Wiseman Development & Management, Inc.', which may or may not be the DRE licensee of record.

findings.title: LA tenant-protection disclosures are lease-and-property obligations, not website obligations — but the site should host them
findings.detail: The City of LA requirements are served and posted at the property, not published on a marketing site. Ordinance 187737 (effective Jan 27 2023) requires landlords to provide a Notice of Renters' Protections to tenants beginning or renewing tenancy on or after that date, and to post it in an accessible common area; failure to post is a misdemeanor under LAMC 151.09.C.9 and 165.05.B.5. LAMC 151.05 requires annual RSO registration and requires serving a copy of the valid registration/renewal statement on the tenant — no landlord may demand or accept rent without it — plus posting the Rent Registration Certificate conspicuously. From Aug 20 2025 landlords must also post and provide the Notice of Right to Counsel at start of tenancy. The Tenant Habitability Plan applies to RSO units undergoing primary renovation. None of this belongs on a property listing page. What belongs on the corporate site is a Residents → Your Rights & Resources hub that links LAHD's official pages and PDFs, explains RSO in plain language, and states plainly that specific unit-level disclosures are provided with the lease. That is a trust asset, not a liability — and it distinguishes a 45-year local operator from a national REIT template.

findings.title: The portfolio spans at least two rent-control jurisdictions — the site must not imply one rule set
findings.detail: Of 72 properties, 71 have City of Los Angeles addresses (including the two Venice properties, which are within the City of LA) and one — Broadway Glendale by Wiseman, 220 E. Broadway, Glendale, CA 91205 — is in the City of Glendale, which has its own rental-rights regime and is outside the LA RSO entirely. One property, Alfred Atlas at 939 N. Alfred Street, sits in ZIP 90069, which straddles the City of Los Angeles and the City of West Hollywood; the address states Los Angeles, but the boundary there is worth confirming since West Hollywood has its own rent stabilization ordinance. Separately, California statewide AB 1482 (Civ. Code 1947.12 rent cap and 1946.2 just cause) applies to properties not covered by stricter local ordinances, and exemption claims require specific statutory notice language delivered as a lease addendum or signed written notice — if that notice is not given, a single-family home or condo is NOT exempt. Implication for the build: a jurisdiction field per property, and any rent-control or tenant-rights content scoped per property rather than stated once globally.

findings.title: California has NO current law requiring all-in advertised rent — the widely repeated claim is false
findings.detail: I checked this because several industry blogs assert it confidently and it would materially change pricing display. leginfo confirms SB 611 (2023-24) was approved by the Governor and filed Sept 19 2024, but its operative provisions are: prohibiting fees for serving or delivering notices, prohibiting fees for paying rent or security deposits by check, and security deposit limits. It contains no advertising or fee-disclosure-in-listings requirement. AB 747 (2025-26) was chaptered Oct 10 2025 as Chapter 563 — it is the Service of Process Accountability, Reform and Equity (SPARE) Act, operative Jan 1 2027, and has nothing to do with rental advertising. The real bill is AB 1248 (Haney), amended to require that for tenancies on or after April 1 2026 a landlord's advertisement include all required fees and charges in addition to rent plus a description of optional housing services and their fees — and it was set aside/held for the year in 2025, opposed successfully by AAGLA and CAA. It is a two-year bill that may return. Separately, SB 478 (Honest Pricing Law, eff. July 1 2024) bars advertising a price for a good or service that excludes mandatory fees; the AG's FAQ does not address long-term residential leases and its scope there is genuinely unsettled. Design the pricing UI to be all-in-ready — show rent plus a clear itemized 'other monthly charges' block — but do not tell the client it is currently required.

findings.title: Spanish-language support is a legal consideration in LA, not just a nicety
findings.detail: California Civil Code 1632 requires a business that negotiates primarily in Spanish, Chinese, Tagalog, Vietnamese or Korean to deliver a translation of the contract — including every term and condition — in that language before execution, and the statute expressly covers leases, subleases, rental contracts or agreements and other terms of tenancy. Non-compliance lets the consumer rescind and seek restitution. This is a lease obligation rather than a website one, and HUD's 2007 Title VI limited-English-proficiency guidance was among the eight documents withdrawn effective Sept 17 2025. But in an LA Westside/Hollywood portfolio, if leasing agents actually negotiate in Spanish, the 1632 obligation attaches regardless. The website implication is modest and worth doing: a Spanish language toggle for the key renter-facing paths (search, property detail, contact, residents hub), proper lang attributes, and — importantly — never machine-translating legal or disclosure text.

findings.title: Resident-facing surface: five destinations, reachable in one click from every page
findings.detail: Industry convergence on the resident stack is clear: online rent payment with autopay, maintenance requests with photo/video upload and status tracking, document storage, messaging, and lease renewal e-sign. The 2026 baseline for maintenance specifically includes in-app submission with photo and short video, urgency tagging, scheduling-window selection, technician ETA, and a post-completion satisfaction survey. For Wiseman — running on Yardi/RentCafe — the portal itself already exists; the website's job is routing and pre-authentication content, which is where stock templates fail. The five destinations: (1) Pay Rent — deep link to the RentCafe resident portal, visible in the primary nav, not buried in a footer; (2) Maintenance Request — with a clearly separated 24/7 emergency path and a phone number, since a resident with a flooding unit should never be asked to log in; (3) Residents hub — move-in guide, utilities setup with the actual LADWP/SoCalGas/Spectrum links (note Motor Tides' CONTENT.md confirms trash, gas, electric and water are tenant responsibility, so this is real information residents need), renters insurance requirements and how to submit proof, parking and package policies, building access; (4) Your Rights & Resources — the LAHD/RSO links described above; (5) Contact your community — per-property office address, hours and direct phone, since the data file already carries a distinct phone per property.

findings.title: Trust signals for a 45-year private operator are different from a REIT's — lean on specificity
findings.detail: Wiseman Residential was founded in 1980 by Isaac Cohanzad, is privately held, vertically integrated (develops and manages in-house), and concentrated in Westside LA submarkets — Brentwood, Venice, West LA, Palms, Culver City, Hollywood, Sawtelle — often using TOC density-bonus incentives with affordable set-asides. Every one of those facts is a trust signal a national template cannot claim, and the stock RentCafe site surfaces none of them. The concrete set worth building: founding year and founder named on an About page (not '45+ years of excellence' as a floating stat); a real Los Angeles corporate office address with map and hours; named leadership with photographs; the DRE licensed entity name and license number; aggregate review ratings with links out to Yelp and Google; published response-time commitments for leasing inquiries and maintenance, which is only credible if it's a number you can actually hold; and the Equal Housing Opportunity mark. On TOC affordable units specifically — if the portfolio includes covenanted income-restricted units, the site should say so plainly and explain how to inquire. Concealing them creates fair-housing exposure; surfacing them is both compliant and a differentiator.

findings.title: Schema.org and local SEO: entity per property, neighborhood pages, one canonical NAP
findings.detail: The right markup for a 72-property portfolio is layered JSON-LD, not a single blob. Site-wide: Organization (or RealEstateAgent) on the homepage with name, logo, url, telephone, address, foundingDate 1980, sameAs links to Yelp/Google/Facebook/LinkedIn. Per property page: ApartmentComplex with name, address (PostalAddress with full street/city/state/postalCode), geo (GeoCoordinates), telephone, numberOfAvailableAccommodationsIn, amenityFeature as LocationFeatureSpecification entries, photo, and containedInPlace pointing to the neighborhood. Per floor plan / available unit: Apartment nested with numberOfRooms, numberOfBathroomsTotal, floorSize (QuantitativeValue in sqft), and an Offer carrying price, priceCurrency USD, availability and availabilityStarts. Use JSON-LD, validate at validator.schema.org, and make sure the schema's NAP matches the Google Business Profile exactly — mismatches are a known trust penalty. For GBP at this scale, each community needs its own profile with a unique local phone number; a single shared number across locations confuses verification. The property data file already carries a distinct phone per property, which is the right foundation. Neighborhood landing pages (/apartments/brentwood/, /apartments/west-la/, /apartments/hollywood/, /apartments/venice/, /apartments/palms/) are the highest-value net-new pages — each listing its properties, with genuinely local non-demographic content, internally linked from every property in that neighborhood.

findings.title: Map vs list is not a choice — and the data can't currently support a map
findings.detail: For a geographically clustered portfolio where neighborhood is the primary decision axis, a synced map+list is the expected pattern: map and results pane bound to the same filter state, hovering a card highlights its pin and vice versa, and the URL encodes filter state so a search is shareable and back-button-safe. The blocker is that properties.psv has no lat/lng — addresses would need geocoding into persisted coordinate columns (do not geocode at runtime; it's slow, rate-limited, and breaks offline builds). Accessibility caveat that matters given the litigation exposure above: a map is not an accessible primary interface. The list must be fully usable and complete on its own, every pin must have a corresponding focusable list item, and the map should be treated as a supplementary view with appropriate ARIA — not the only path to inventory. Saved favorites should work without forcing account creation (localStorage first, with optional sign-in to sync), since a mandatory account before browsing is a well-known drop-off point.

summary:
Wiseman Residential is the consumer-facing brand of a small, family-run Westside LA multifamily developer/manager controlled by the Cohanzad family (Isaac, Benjamin, Michael Cohanzad). The strongest verifiable facts: the company's own Archinect firm profile says it was "Established in 1985 by Isaac W. Cohanzad" and has "built 1000+ residential units"; the BBB profile for the related entity "Wiseman Development & Management, Inc." (alternate names: Copac Corp, Wiseman Development, Wiseman Residential) lists a business start date of 6/28/1987; and California's CSLB shows an active Class B general-building contractor license (#417744) held by COBUILD INC at 11601 Santa Monica Blvd with Isaac Wise Cohanzad as qualifying individual, originally issued 02/03/1982. Nothing I could find supports "over 45 years."
