Specificity detail worth carrying: the reduced-motion rules are written as `.mask .lock` (two-class descendant, specificity 0-2-0) while the base rule is `.lock` (0-1-0), so the media-query block wins on specificity, and `!important` only covers inline styles. Writing the override as bare `.lock` inside the media query would NOT beat the inline style without `!important`.

findings.title: option-e is the only concept with externalized CSS/JS — and it is already a design system
findings.detail:
`option-e/style.css` (579 lines) and `option-e/app.js` (438 lines) are shared across four pages; every other concept inlines everything into each HTML file. For a multi-page corporate site with ~72 property pages, option-e is the only viable starting point — the inline concepts would mean 72 copies of the stylesheet.

Tokens (style.css:13-37): a flat `:root` block of 15 design tokens (`--paper`, `--paper-2`, `--ink`, `--ink-soft`, `--mist`, `--sand-ink`, `--rule`, `--rule-soft`, `--sand`, `--teal`, `--night`, `--cream`, `--serif`, `--sans`, `--ease`) plus layout tokens (`--vh100`, `--pad:clamp(22px,3.8vw,92px)`, `--edge`, `--wordsY`) plus the ten `--mtc-*` chat tokens. Six themes are defined purely as `[data-theme="x"]{...}` token overrides at style.css:476-547 with the comment 'structure untouched.' This is exactly the right shape for a corporate site that needs per-property or per-region accents.

Generic and directly liftable from app.js:
  • Lenis setup (7-19): `new Lenis({lerp:0.085})` guarded by `!reduce && window.Lenis`, single rAF loop, plus `scrollToY()` with a duration derived from distance (`Math.min(2.8, Math.max(1.2, Math.abs(y-scrollY)/innerHeight*1.1))`) and a cubic in-out easing. Falls back to native `scrollTo({behavior:reduce?'auto':'smooth'})` when Lenis is absent.
  • Anchor interception (21-31) that handles both `#id` and `page.html#id` forms by comparing `url.pathname !== location.pathname`.
  • Page-transition curtain (34-58): injects the brand lockup into `.pt`, intercepts same-origin non-hash non-`_blank` links, adds `.cover`, navigates after 950ms. CSS at style.css:456-471.
  • Reveal observers (161-172): two IntersectionObservers — `.rv/.split` at `threshold:.14, rootMargin:'0px 0px -8% 0px'`, and `.imgrv` at `threshold:0.001` (images need to start decoding early). Both `unobserve` after firing.
  • Fullscreen menu (105-129) with the best accessibility work in the repo: toggles `aria-expanded`, `aria-hidden`, `body.menu-open`, applies `inert` to main/footer, calls `lenis.stop()/start()`, moves focus to the close button and returns it to the trigger, and closes on Escape.
  • Smart header (376-403): transparent above 110px; adds `.hd` (translateY(-102%)) scrolling down, `.frost` scrolling up; the 6px hysteresis threshold prevents flicker.
  • Section stepper + `landY()` (340-372).

Concept-specific, leave behind: the chapter-word dual-layer sweep (175-212), the hero letter-splitter (131-159), sliders (214-245), tours strip (247-265), floor-plan preview (267-296), map interactions (298-322), experience rail (324-337), and the theme-switcher UI (60-101, which is explicitly labeled a 'concept review' control).

findings.title: The two non-obvious measurement tricks in option-e's stepper — copy these verbatim
findings.detail:
Both are documented by inline comments and both solve bugs that are very hard to diagnose after the fact.

1. **`absTop()` instead of `getBoundingClientRect()`** (app.js:344-345). The comment: 'transform-free layout position: entrance reveals (.rv/.split) shift rects at measure time.' Since `.rv` applies `transform:translateY(24px)` until it reveals (style.css:53), any rect-based measurement of a not-yet-revealed section is off by the reveal offset. `absTop` walks `offsetTop`/`offsetParent` instead, which transforms do not affect:
```js
function absTop(el){ var t = 0; while(el){ t += el.offsetTop; el = el.offsetParent; } return t; }
```
Any scroll-spy, stepper, or anchor-landing code in a site that also uses transform-based reveals must use this, not `getBoundingClientRect().top + scrollY`. Note `stopTop()` at line 343 DOES use rects — it is only used for coarse 'has this section passed the probe' comparisons where the 24px error is irrelevant.

2. **`landY()` centers the content block, not the section top** (346-360). It finds the heading, measures down to the inner wrapper's content edge (subtracting `paddingBottom`), clamps to the section bottom, then: 'center the block when it fits; otherwise pin the heading 96px from the top' — `blockH <= innerHeight - 144 ? top - Math.max(72,(innerHeight-blockH)/2) : top - 96`. This is why anchor landings in option-e feel composed rather than jammed against the viewport top.

3. **Deep-link correction survives late layout shifts** (app.js:416-428). When `location.hash` is present it re-runs `hashFix` on `requestAnimationFrame`, on `document.fonts.ready`, and on `load` — because 'fonts and gallery images shift layout as they load.' Crucially it is gated by a `hashDone` flag set by one-shot `wheel`/`touchstart` listeners, so a user who has already started scrolling is never yanked back. For a 72-property site with heavy imagery and deep links from a portfolio index, this is essential.

A related pattern in the chapter sweep (app.js:208-212): `sizeMasks()` is re-run on `resize` AND on `document.fonts.ready`, because the mask geometry depends on `ink.offsetHeight`, which changes when the display face swaps in.

findings.title: The header's light/dark adaptation is driven by a `data-sec` contract on every section
findings.detail:
Every top-level section carries `data-sec="light"` or `data-sec="dark"` (option-e/index.html:67,79,89,114,124,149,159,184; residences.html:66,74,107,114,149,162). This single attribute drives three things in `onScroll()` (app.js:393-403, 405-415):

  • The header probes 60px below the scroll position, walks the `stops` array to find the last section whose top has passed, and toggles `.on-light` — `.site-header.on-light{color:var(--ink);text-shadow:none}` (style.css:87). Default header state is `color:var(--cream)` with `text-shadow:0 1px 16px rgba(14,39,38,.35)` for legibility over photography (style.css:72,86).
  • A special case at app.js:401: if the section under the header is a chapter-curtain (`.chc`) whose `dataset.reveal` is still below 0.8, it is treated as 'light' regardless — because the sweep has not yet flipped the words. This coupling between the sweep progress and the header color is the kind of detail that looks broken if omitted.
  • The stepper button probes at `scrollY + innerHeight - 48` (bottom of viewport, since the button lives there) and toggles its own `.on-light`, which adds a frosted backdrop (style.css:166).

For a corporate site this contract is worth keeping verbatim: any full-bleed photographic band is `data-sec="dark"`, any paper section is `data-sec="light"`, and the header never needs per-page configuration.

One more header nuance (app.js:377-379, 386): the header un-hides on `focusin` and refuses to hide while `hdr.matches(':focus-within')` or while `body.menu-open` — so keyboard users are never chasing a header that slides away under them.

findings.title: Chat widget API: ten CSS custom properties, seven allowlisted launcher variants, flat flow functions behind one keyword router
findings.detail:
`assets/chat.js` (778 lines, zero dependencies, IIFE, self-appending to `document.body`).

**Theming** (chat.js:18-29). A `THEME` object maps each knob to a `var(--mtc-x, fallback)` string, and those strings are interpolated into a `.mtc-root{--_a:...;--_ai:...}` rule at line 55. So the widget reads authored tokens once into private `--_*` variables. The ten knobs: `--mtc-accent`, `--mtc-accent-ink`, `--mtc-surface`, `--mtc-ink`, `--mtc-muted`, `--mtc-bubble-bot`, `--mtc-bubble-user`, `--mtc-bubble-user-ink`, `--mtc-radius`, `--mtc-font`. Every one has a sensible teal default, so the widget works unthemed. Themes set them alongside the site tokens — see option-e/style.css:28-36 (base) and each `[data-theme]` block (e.g. 484-485, 516-517, 546) which re-declares the `--mtc-*` set. Because they resolve at paint time, switching `[data-theme]` restyles the live chat panel with no JS.

**Launcher selection** (chat.js:31-41). Resolution order: `?chat=` URL param → `window.MTC_VARIANT` → `'minimal'`. Then a set of aliases is normalized (`bubble→minimal`, `pet|mascot|wave→logo`, `beacon→lighthouse`, `eyes|face|chatty→buddy`, `human|maya|photo→agent`, `label|text→pill`), and finally an allowlist regex `/^(minimal|robot|lighthouse|buddy|logo|agent|pill)$/` clamps anything unrecognized back to `minimal`. This is proper input hygiene on a URL param — keep it. Concepts opt in with `<script>window.MTC_VARIANT='pill';</script>` immediately before the script tag (option-e/index.html:241-242).

**Flow structure** (chat.js:543-660). Every flow is a bare function that chains `bot(html, delayMs)` promises and ends by calling `chips([...])` or `mainChips()`. `bot()` (510-520) shows a typing indicator 260ms in and resolves after the stated delay. `chips()` (522-533) renders quick-reply buttons whose `f` property is the next flow function. `MAIN_CHIPS` (660-666) is a five-entry array of `{t: label, f: flowFn}`. Flows present: `flowPricing`, `flowTour` (with a `pickTime`/`confirmTour` two-step sub-flow), `flowPets`, `flowAmenities`, `flowHood`, `flowApply`, `flowUtilities`, `flowHours`, `flowLocation`, `flowParking`, and `fallback`.

**Router** (chat.js:649-669). A flat ladder of `if (/regex/.test(t)) return flowX;` over the lowercased input, ending in `return fallback`. First match wins, so ordering matters (`/\b(price|pricing|cost|rent|how much|rate|special|deal|month)/` is first).

**Property data** (chat.js:343-351): a module-level `PLANS` array of `{n,b,s,p,a}`. Plus three module constants at 48-50: `APPLY_URL`, `TEL`, `TEL_LABEL`.

**Environment guards worth keeping**: `REDUCED` and `FINE_POINTER` are both read through try/catch `matchMedia` (43-46); input is only auto-focused on a fine pointer (openPanel, so mobile keyboards don't spring up); the teaser chime arms an AudioContext on the first `pointerdown`/`keydown` and only stands down once `state === 'running'`, replaying a pending chime if the teaser is still on screen (chat.js:~724-750). Teaser appears at 5200ms and auto-hides at 26000ms.

findings.title: Re-scripting the chat widget for a corporate/portfolio site: what actually has to change
findings.detail:
The engine is property-agnostic; only the content layer is hardcoded. Concretely, to turn it into a Wiseman Residential portfolio concierge:

**Mechanically unchanged**: the style block (55-388), the launcher/teaser/badge/panel scaffold, `bot()`/`chips()`/`addMsg()`/`showTyping()`, the variant allowlist, open/close and focus handling, the audio arming, the reduced-motion and pointer guards. That is roughly 600 of the 778 lines.

**Must change**:
  1. `PLANS` (343-351) → a `PROPERTIES` array. The data already exists at `/Users/wangzhen/Documents/wiseman website/corporate/data/properties.psv` — 72 rows, pipe-separated, columns `name|category|beds|baths|sqft|address|price|phone|path|image`. Note `category` already encodes neighborhood (23 West LA, 23 Hollywood, 18 unlabeled 'Apartment', 6 Brentwood, 1 Culver City, 1 'Condo, West LA'), which is the natural first branch of a portfolio flow.
  2. The single `APPLY_URL` and `TEL`/`TEL_LABEL` constants (48-50) become per-property — each row in the PSV carries its own `phone` and RentCafe `path`. `flowApply`, `flowParking`, `flowHours` and `fallback` all interpolate `TEL_LABEL` and would need the currently-selected property threaded through.
  3. The greeting in `openPanel()` hardcodes 'Welcome to Motor Tides by Wiseman... Brand-new 2 & 3 bedroom homes... from $3,770/mo'. A corporate greeting should lead with the portfolio ('72 communities across LA, 45 years') and the first question becomes *which* property or *which* neighborhood.
  4. `flowLocation` (630-634) hardcodes one address and one Maps URL — becomes a per-property lookup.

**Must be ADDED** — this is the real work, and it is a structural change, not a copy edit. The current flow graph is stateless: every flow returns to `mainChips()`. A portfolio concierge needs one piece of conversation state — the selected property — and a new entry flow that establishes it (by neighborhood, by bedroom count, or by budget). Realistically: a `var selected = null;` module variable, a `flowFindHome()` that filters `PROPERTIES` and renders result cards, a `selectProperty(p)` setter, and then making the existing property-specific flows (`flowPricing`, `flowTour`, `flowApply`, `flowLocation`, `flowHours`, `flowParking`) read from `selected` and fall back to asking which community when it is null. The router ladder also needs a neighborhood branch (`/\b(west la|hollywood|brentwood|venice|glendale|culver)/`) ahead of the generic location match, and property names would ideally be matched by scanning the PROPERTIES array rather than by regex.

Estimate: the engine is untouched, the data layer is a PSV parse, and the flow rewrite is maybe 150-200 lines. The card renderer in `flowPricing` (550-554) already produces a `.mtc-card` list and is directly reusable as a property-result renderer.

findings.title: Deploy pipeline: prep_deploy.py builds N independent static bundles, each with a vercel.json that rewrites images to the RentCafe CDN
findings.detail:
`scripts/prep_deploy.py` (144 lines, stdlib only — `json`, `os`, `shutil`). It is a generator, not a build tool: no minification, no bundling, no hashing.

**Constants**: `ROOT` is an absolute hardcoded path to the redesign dir (line 11) — this will need editing for a new site, it is not repo-relative. `OUT = ROOT/deploy`. `HUB_URL` plus a `CONCEPT_URL` dict of 10 project→URL mappings (14-26).

**Image strategy** (28-70). `CDN = "https://resource.rentcafe.com/image/upload/{t}/s3/2/9707/{f}"` where `{t}` is a Cloudinary-style transform string — three presets: `PHOTO_T = "q_auto,f_auto,c_limit,w_1800"`, `PLAN_T = "...,w_1200"`, `LOGO_T = "...,w_400"`. `MAP` is a 33-entry dict mapping a clean local filename (`hero-living.jpg`) to `(transform, ugly_percent_encoded_cdn_filename)` — e.g. `"motor%20tides%20-%20unit%20705%20-%20kithcenm%20small%20dining,%20lr,%20and%20patio_final.jpg"`. This is the whole point of the design: the HTML references clean local names, works offline against bundled images, and on Vercel the same paths resolve to the CDN.

`vercel_json()` (72-80) emits `{"rewrites":[{"source":"/assets/img/<name>","destination":"<cdn url>"}]}`. **Critical gotcha, documented at line 73**: 'Vercel's router treats "(" ")" in destinations as regex groups; percent-encode them' — `.replace("(","%28").replace(")","%29")`. Many RentCafe filenames contain parentheses.

**Build** (82-135): `shutil.rmtree(OUT)` then rebuild. The hub gets `option-<k>/index.html` hrefs rewritten to absolute concept URLs (a `.replace` on the prefix only, so `?chat=` query strings survive — noted in the comment at line 91). Each concept dir: HTML files get three rewrites — `../assets/chat.js`→`/chat.js`, `../assets/img/`→`/assets/img/`, `href="../index.html"`→`href="<HUB_URL>/"` (both quote styles) — non-HTML files (css, js) are copied verbatim; `assets/img/plans-trim/` is copied in; the shared `chat.js` is written to each project root; `vercel.json` is written.

**Sanity check** (137-142): after building, it greps every output HTML for surviving `../assets` or `../index.html` and prints `OK` or `PROBLEMS: [...]`. Then prints a size manifest for every file.

**Deployment** is manual per project (README): `cd deploy/<key>; vercel link --yes --project motor-tides-concept-<key> --scope <scope>; vercel deploy --prod --yes`. `redesign/deploy/` is gitignored (.gitignore:9-10) and must be regenerated before every deploy. Per MEMORY.md, the Vercel MCP token cannot create projects — new projects must be created via CLI.

findings.title: House conventions and traps, part 1: layout and CSS
findings.detail:
Each of these is either stated in a comment or provable from a commit that fixed it.

**1. `overflow-x:clip`, never `overflow-x:hidden`.** Every concept sets it on both `html` and `body` (option-monogram:21,23; option-grandtour:21,23; option-voyage:21,23; option-e/style.css:44). This is not stylistic — `overflow:hidden` on an ancestor creates a scroll container that silently breaks `position:sticky`. Since the mask stage, the curtains, and the journey rail all depend on sticky/fixed positioning, using `hidden` would kill the entire scroll choreography with no error message.

**2. The shorthand-padding gutter trap.** The universal reset is `*{margin:0;padding:0;box-sizing:border-box}` (option-monogram:20) and the gutter comes from `.wrap{padding:0 var(--pad)}` (option-monogram:51). The discipline that follows is 100% consistent across the codebase and must be inherited: **an element that carries the `.wrap` class uses `padding-top`/`padding-bottom` longhand only**; a full-bleed background section uses `padding: X 0` shorthand and puts an inner `<div class="wrap">` inside it. Verify: `.mani` (72), `.inside` (91), `.close` (135) are all `padding-top`/`padding-bottom` longhand, and their markup is `class="mani wrap"` (239), `class="inside wrap"` (254), `class="close wrap"` (302). Meanwhile `.pindex{background:var(--deep);...;padding:clamp(70px,9vw,130px) 0}` (104) uses shorthand — and its markup at line 267-268 is `<section class="pindex">` with a nested `<div class="wrap">`. Writing `padding: 80px 0` on a `.wrap` element silently zeroes the horizontal gutter and the text runs to the viewport edge.

**3. `vh` needs an `svh` twin for anything pinned.** option-e does this correctly: `--vh100:100vh` at :root then `@supports (height:100svh){:root{--vh100:100svh;--wordsY:36svh}}` (style.css:22,38), and every curtain height is re-declared in svh inside an `@supports` block (127). Mobile URL-bar show/hide changes `vh` and makes pinned stages jump. option-monogram does NOT do this (its stage is plain `100vh`, line 79) — fix that when porting.

**4. Flex buttons need `min-width:max-content`, not a pixel min-width.** Commit 8d1757b: `.btn-line`/`.btn-fill` had `flex:1` + `min-width:150px` + `white-space:nowrap` + `overflow:hidden`; 'Check availability' needs 209px, so between ~312px and ~430px container width each button was squeezed to 150px and the label clipped by up to 59px. Fix: `flex:1 1 auto` with `min-width:max-content`. Verified across a 280-640px sweep.

**5. Masked line reveals must clear descenders.** Commit d42b039: an `overflow:hidden` line-rise mask with `line-height:1.02` cut 0.098em off descenders (the 'y' and comma in 'One day,') — 4.7px at 48px mobile, ~12.5px at the 8rem desktop max. Fix: extend the mask `0.16em` below the line box and cancel with an equal negative margin, then push the start offset from 112% to 125% so the taller mask still hides the text. This is exactly what option-e/style.css:58-59 encodes: `.words .o,.split .o{display:block;overflow:hidden;padding-bottom:.14em;margin-bottom:-.14em}`. The audit covered all 24 concept pages; only Grand Tour was affected because Monogram's headings are uppercase.

**6. Non-positioned text paints below any positioned z-index≥0 sibling.** option-grandtour/index.html:81 carries the comment verbatim: 'hero copy sits above the sun: non-positioned text otherwise paints below any positioned z-index>=0 element' (commit fd7970a).

findings.title: House conventions and traps, part 2: color, contrast, motion, and caching
findings.detail:
**7. Interpolated palettes must never let ink cross a low-contrast midpoint.** option-grandtour/index.html:377-386 — the `mix()` function lerps background and deep colors channel-by-channel but SNAPS ink and accent at the halfway seam: `var inkFrom = t < 0.5 ? pa : pb;` with the comment 'ink must never pass through a low-contrast midpoint: snap it at the seam.' Lerping dark-ink-on-cream toward cream-ink-on-dark passes through grey-on-grey. Additionally, `t` is remapped `clamp01((t-0.35)/0.3)` at line 414 to 'hold each chapter's palette through its middle; blend in the seams', so the blend happens fast, in the transition zone, rather than continuously.

**8. Display type over photography: stroke, not offset shadow.** Commit c97322d: gold fill over photography read badly on bright backgrounds; the fix was cream fill + thin gold `-webkit-text-stroke` with `paint-order:stroke fill`. The reasoning is specific and worth inheriting — 'Chose a stroke over a hard-offset gold shadow because the chapter words are revealed by a moving clip window — an offset shadow ghosts at the clip edge, while a stroke stays registered to each glyph.' Implementation at option-e/style.css:490 with a `@media (max-width:640px)` thinning to 0.4px (492-494) and an `@supports not (-webkit-text-stroke:...)` text-shadow fallback (495-497). Follow-up commit 3637ebf then LIGHTENED the shadows: two warm-brown shadows 'rang every cream letter with a muddy halo — most visible on mobile, where Cormorant's hairlines sit at ~47px.' Rule: the scrim establishes contrast; per-glyph shadow gives only gentle local separation, never a second outline.

**9. Body copy stays on the AA-safe neutral even when display type goes brand-colored.** option-e/style.css:487 comment: 'gold owns the display type; body copy stays on the AA neutral --ink'. The themes carry a paired `--sand` (decorative) and `--sand-ink` (text-safe, darker) — e.g. gilded `--sand:#D0AF58; --sand-ink:#755409`. Commit c97322d records 'Gold on light paper (.cw.ink) is unchanged at 6.64:1.' Two-token accent pairs are the convention; do not use the decorative token for text.

**10. Dark themes are a token inversion PLUS an explicit hover-state sweep.** `[data-theme="midnight"]` (style.css:541-568) inverts `--paper`/`--ink` — but then needs ~15 follow-up rules because every element whose hover state was 'fill with --ink, text goes --cream' now needs `color:var(--night)` instead: `.pill:hover`, `.btn-line:hover`, `.btn-fill:hover`, `.csl-btn:hover`, `.hero-jump:hover`, `.skip-link`, `.socials a:hover`, plus SVG `fill` overrides for map labels and an override for the chat launcher. Budget for this sweep; a token flip alone produces invisible hover text.

**11. Reduced motion collapses choreography but keeps composition.** Every concept has a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)` block (option-monogram:153-162; option-e/style.css:65,120,151,160,310,468) and every JS entry point reads `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` once and branches. Two patterns: option-e's `if(reduce)` branch for the chapter sweep sets a static end-state (`clipPath:'none'`, hides the ink layer) then empties the array so the per-frame loop does no work (app.js:203-207); grandtour swaps the interpolated palette for a per-chapter IntersectionObserver (option-grandtour:366-372). Note the inverse guard also exists — `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference)` gates the stepper's idle drift animation (style.css:171).

**12. Cache-busting is a hand-maintained query param, and it can drift.** Assets are referenced as `style.css?v=47`, `app.js?v=31`, `chat.js?v=4` (option-e/index.html:11,241-242). The trap: `prep_deploy.py` writes the SAME current `assets/chat.js` into every deploy project, but each HTML page carries its own hardcoded `?v=` number — and the archived a/b/c pages still request `?chat.js?v=2` while receiving the v4 file. Returning visitors keep the stale cached copy. If a new site keeps this scheme, bump every referencing page when a shared asset changes, or better, have prep_deploy stamp the version from a file hash.

**13. `.js` class gating.** `<script>document.documentElement.classList.add('js')</script>` sits inline in `<head>` (option-e/index.html:12), and all reveal rules are written `.js .rv{opacity:0;...}` (style.css:52-56). Content is visible by default and only hidden once JS is confirmed — no flash of invisible content if the script fails.

**14. Mobile header crowding is a known repeat offender.** Commit 37e459f: 'a header bug shared by every concept: the brand lockup and the CTA both wrapped to two lines inside a 62px bar.' Fix was `nowrap` + tighter sizing under 430px, with all rules `max-width`-scoped so desktop is untouched. Check the header at 375px on day one.

findings.title: Secondary mechanics worth knowing: Voyage's damped traversal and Grand Tour's palette rail
findings.detail:
Both are single-file inline concepts, so porting means extracting, but the mechanics are small and distinctive.

**Voyage damped traversal** (option-voyage/index.html:413, 486-499). Elements carry `data-tr="x0,y0,r0,x1,y1,r1,speed"` in vw/vh/deg. Per frame, for each object: compute section progress `p = clamp01((innerHeight - r.top)/(innerHeight + r.height))`, derive a target `clamp01(0.5 + (p-0.5)*speed*2)`, then damp toward it with `d.cur += (target - d.cur) * 0.075` and write a single `translate3d(Xvw,Yvh,0) rotate(Rdeg)`. The damping constant is what gives the drift its weight — it is not scroll-linked, it chases the scroll. Note this runs in an unconditional `requestAnimationFrame` loop (503) rather than a scroll-gated one, because damping needs frames even when scrolling has stopped; the scroll-derived work is guarded by `if(y !== lastScrollY)` (440) so only the damping runs when idle. That split is the reusable idea.

**Voyage journey rail** (49-59 CSS, 421-423 + 448-458 JS). A fixed left rail: a 2px track with a `transform:scaleY(p)` fill (never height, so it composites), a live percentage readout with `font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums` to stop digit jitter, and six leg labels revealed on `:hover`/`:focus-within`. Active leg is whichever section has `r.top < innerHeight*0.55 && r.bottom > innerHeight*0.35`. Hidden under 900px entirely; labels hidden under 1250px (59-60). For a 72-property portfolio this is a plausible chassis for a region or decade rail.

**Grand Tour palette rail** (option-grandtour/index.html:353-364, 403-420). Chapters carry `data-pal="hex,hex,hex,hex"`; the hexes are parsed once into RGB triples at load. Per frame, find the segment by comparing a probe at `scrollY + innerHeight*0.5` against chapter CENTERS (not tops), compute t, remap it to blend only in the seams, mix, and write four `document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--bgv'|'--inkv'|'--acv'|'--deepv', 'rgb(...)')`. Because everything downstream uses `color-mix(in srgb, var(--inkv) 22%, transparent)` for rules and borders, the whole page re-tints from four writes. Note `body{...transition:none}` at line 23 is deliberate: a transition on body color would fight the per-frame writes.

findings.title: Shared per-page baseline every concept implements (the a11y/structure floor)
findings.detail:
Stated in README.md:120-127 and verifiable in each file. A new page in this repo is expected to have all of:

  • A skip link — `.skip-link{position:absolute;left:-9999px;top:0;...}` with `.skip-link:focus{left:12px;top:12px}` (option-monogram:47-48; option-e/style.css:47-48).
  • A keyboard-navigable header with visible focus — `a:focus-visible,button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:3px}` (option-monogram:26). Themes override the outline color where the default fails on their paper (e.g. style.css:509).
  • A hamburger menu under 760px. Two implementations: option-e's is authored in HTML with full `inert`/focus management (app.js:105-129), while the inline concepts BUILD it in JS from the existing `.hnav` links (option-monogram:465-493) — it clones hrefs and `aria-current`, appends a `.mnav` overlay, toggles `body.style.overflow`, and closes on link click or Escape. The JS-built version is less accessible (no `inert`, no focus return) — prefer option-e's.
  • A branded page-transition curtain. Same pattern in both places: inject brand markup into `.pt`, intercept same-origin links, `.cover`, navigate after 950ms, and critically `addEventListener('pageshow', e => { if(e.persisted) pt.classList.remove('cover') })` so a bfcache back-navigation never leaves the page covered by an opaque panel (option-e/app.js:54-57; option-monogram:500). The inline version additionally bails on `e.metaKey||e.ctrlKey||e.shiftKey||e.defaultPrevented` (option-monogram:507) so cmd-click still opens a new tab — option-e's version does NOT check modifier keys, which is a small bug worth not inheriting.
  • One rAF loop per page, IntersectionObserver for reveals, transform/opacity only for motion.
  • `<script src="../assets/chat.js?v=N" defer>` preceded by `window.MTC_VARIANT`.

Footer contract (CONTENT.md:118): '© 2026 Wiseman Residential · Equal Housing Opportunity' plus resident-login and a concept attribution line. For a corporate site the Equal Housing Opportunity mark is a legal requirement, not decoration.

findings.title: Brand assets and content-accuracy discipline that carry to the corporate site
findings.detail:
CONTENT.md opens with a standing rule: 'Use it verbatim or lightly polished. NEVER invent prices, unit counts, or contact info.' Both READMEs close with the same two caveats — the floor-plan-drawing-to-plan-name mapping is INFERRED and unconfirmed by Wiseman, and pricing/availability is a point-in-time snapshot with the live leasing system as authority. Every concept links out to SecureCafe/RentCafe rather than restating. A 72-property corporate site multiplies this risk by 72; the same rule should govern.

Brand assets already established (CONTENT.md:17-27):
  • The mark is three teal vertical bars with angled bottom edges rising to the right, wordmark 'WISEMAN' letterspaced ~0.35em beneath, light weight.
  • The preferred implementation is an inline SVG using `currentColor` so it inverts on dark sections — three `<polygon>` elements in a `0 0 100 100` viewBox: `14,18 34,18 34,74 14,80` / `40,18 60,18 60,71 40,77` / `66,18 86,18 86,68 66,74`. This exact markup appears in every header and every page-transition curtain (option-e/index.html:22-26, app.js:37-40).
  • Core colors: deep teal #074B4D, teal #0E6B72 / #1C6775, accent sand-yellow #FEDA77, ink #202020, white. The current live site uses Montserrat / Open Sans / Mulish.
  • Corporate positioning line already recorded: 'With over forty-five years of experience, we design our properties with Los Angeles' savvy renter in mind.'
  • Corporate social/links: facebook.com/Officialwisemanresidential, instagram.com/wisemanresidential, yelp.com/biz/wiseman-residential-los-angeles-2, wisemanresidential.com.

The Voyage bars animation (option-voyage:472-483) is worth noting as an existing brand-motion idea: the three logo bars rise and lock into place with a staggered lag (`lag = clamp01(bp*(1.35+i*0.28) - i*0.22)`, smoothstepped), using `transformBox:'fill-box'` so each polygon transforms about its own box. That is a ready-made corporate-identity moment.
